boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten campus places with documented uses for studying, creating, meeting, relaxing, recreation and experiencing art at Stan State’s Turlock campus.

cards.title: Choose Your Own Study Volume
cards.subtitle: Quiet seats, group rooms and computer workstations
cards.notes: Pick a quiet area for solo work or reserve a group study room when conversation and shared screens are part of the assignment.
cards.short_summary: A flexible study base with quiet areas, reservable rooms, computers and research help under one roof.
cards.evidence_claim: The university states that Vasché Library provides computer workstations, wireless internet, quiet study seats and reservable group study rooms throughout the building.
cards.access_notes: Library access and room reservations are governed by current university library policies; verify eligibility and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Bring the Course That Needs a Second Pass
cards.subtitle: Peer-led learning support in Vasché Library L222
cards.notes: Schedule tutoring or drop in for available support, then use the nearby study area to apply the feedback while the material is fresh.
cards.short_summary: An academic-support space combining tutoring, writing help, supplemental instruction and practical study resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Commons identifies L222 in Vasché Library as its campus location and offers peer-led support through tutoring, writing and supplemental instruction.
cards.access_notes: Services are offered in person and online; appointment and drop-in availability varies, so consult StanTutor before arriving.

cards.title: Talk Through a Draft Before Revising It
cards.subtitle: Collaborative writing support in Vasché Library L221
cards.notes: Bring a draft, prompt or early idea to a tutoring session and identify one revision goal before returning to your regular study spot.
cards.short_summary: A focused place for students to work collaboratively with tutors on writing at any stage of the process.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says the Writing Center in Vasché Library L221 works collaboratively with undergraduate and graduate students on focus, organization, development and sentence-level concerns.
cards.access_notes: Current students may book available sessions through StanTutor; in-person and online schedules change by academic term.

cards.title: Find Community Beyond the Classroom
cards.subtitle: Dialogue and belonging space in Vasché Library
cards.notes: Stop by to learn about current programs, community conversations and ways to participate; respect posted capacity and event guidelines.
cards.short_summary: A student-facing center created for belonging, intercultural learning, critical dialogue and community building.
cards.evidence_claim: The university documents the Warrior Cross Cultural Center as a Vasché Library space supporting belonging, critical dialogue and action across student backgrounds.
cards.source_title: Warrior Cross Cultural Center Celebrates New Library Space
cards.access_notes: The center serves the campus community; check its current program calendar and operating access before planning a visit.

cards.title: Turn a Prototype Into Something You Can Hold
cards.subtitle: Hands-on making in Vasché Library L259
cards.notes: Arrive with a one-off design or learning project, ask staff about the appropriate equipment and review material rules before making.
cards.short_summary: A supervised creative workspace for prototyping, personal projects and learning fabrication skills through direct practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Warrior Fab Lab policy says its resources support one-off fabrication, prototyping and educational learning, with users creating their own designs with staff assistance.
cards.access_notes: Located in Vasché Library L259. Review current hours, equipment training requirements and prohibited materials before visiting.

cards.title: Use the Steps as a Shared Campus Room
cards.subtitle: Tiered event and gathering space inside the Student Center
cards.notes: Meet on the tiered seating for an informal conversation or check the Student Center schedule for a programmed activity on the stage.
cards.short_summary: A large, tiered Student Center venue that connects two floors and doubles as an entertainment and gathering space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center identifies Warrior Steps as a 3,100-square-foot entertainment space spanning its first and second floors, with stage and audiovisual features.
cards.access_notes: Casual access depends on Student Center operations and scheduled events; organized use may require a reservation.

cards.title: Take a Study Break Over a Table Game
cards.subtitle: Student Center seating, views, pool and foosball
cards.notes: Use the seating for a study pause or meet friends for pool or foosball, while keeping pathways and active game areas clear.
cards.short_summary: A large Student Center gathering area where seating and table games support breaks between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The university’s Student Center opening coverage documents Warrior Grill seating for 410 and describes students using its pool and foosball games for study breaks.
cards.source_title: Stan State Celebrates New Student Center Opening
cards.access_notes: Enter during current Student Center operating hours; food purchases are optional, and game availability may vary.

cards.title: See What Campus Groups Are Setting Up
cards.subtitle: Outdoor activity space beside the Student Center
cards.notes: Walk through between classes to encounter registered organizations and campus activities; give reserved setups room to operate.
cards.short_summary: A prominent outdoor campus space used by student organizations, departments and other groups for programmed activity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center describes the Stan State Quad as a high-traffic campus location reservable by registered student organizations, campus departments and private parties.
cards.access_notes: The outdoor space may be reserved for events; follow temporary signs, event boundaries and campus access rules.

cards.title: Fit a Contemporary-Art Stop Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Exhibition space in the Theatre Building lobby
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition, spend time with one work and use the gallery’s educational setting to frame a conversation afterward.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus gallery presenting contemporary art as a setting for viewing, discussion and cultural exploration.
cards.evidence_claim: The university says the University Art Gallery in the Theatre Building lobby provides direct contemporary-art viewing and educational interaction with exhibitions and artists.
cards.access_notes: Visit during posted gallery hours and confirm the current exhibition schedule; reception parking rules differ from ordinary campus parking.

cards.title: Build Movement Into the Middle of the Day
cards.subtitle: Fitness, court, track, field, climbing and aquatics spaces
cards.notes: Choose the facility that fits your plan, then confirm membership, training, reservation and equipment rules before beginning an activity.
cards.short_summary: A multi-part recreation destination with indoor fitness areas and documented outdoor, climbing and aquatic facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation documents the Student Recreation Complex exterior, weight and cardio rooms, recreation court, track, fields, climbing structure and aquatics facility.
cards.access_notes: Access varies by facility, membership and program. Check current Campus Recreation hours, closures and participation requirements.
